title: The Office - Interview Skills 9 - Asking For Information About The Position
audio: mp3/259. The Office - Interview Skills 9 - Asking For Information About The Position.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and you've been with us for a little while.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，你和我们在一起有一段时间了。

segments.en: You've probably heard some of our interview series already.
segments.zh: 您可能已经听说过我们的一些采访系列。

segments.en: Well this is one of the later episodes in that series.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是该系列的后续剧集之一。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We're at part number nine.
segments.zh: 我们在第九部分。

segments.en: We're reaching the end of our interview and on this occasion we're going to ask our employer a little bit of more information about the company and more importantly about the job.
segments.zh: 我们即将结束面试，在这个场合，我们将向我们的雇主询问更多关于公司的信息，更重要的是关于这项工作。

segments.en: Well this is a very important step.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个非常重要的步骤。

segments.en: Like you say, it's at the end of the interview so we're going to find out more details about the job.
segments.zh: 就像你说的，这是在面试结束时，所以我们将了解有关这项工作的更多细节。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 让我们听听今天的对话。

segments.en: We'll be back in a moment to talk more about it.
segments.zh: 我们稍后会回来讨论更多。

segments.en: Could you tell me a little about the organization?
segments.zh: 你能告诉我一些关于这个组织的信息吗？

segments.en: For example, how big is your office here?
segments.zh: 例如，您的办公室有多大？

segments.en: Well in total we have around 150 employees based in Hong Kong with another 400 in our head office in Beijing.
segments.zh: 总的来说，我们在香港有大约150名员工，另外还有400名在北京的总部。

segments.en: The news desk staff in Hong Kong has around 80 staff.
segments.zh: 香港的新闻台工作人员约有80名员工。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: And how about the working hours?
segments.zh: 工作时间怎么样？

segments.en: Well as you know Rebecca, in journalism work hours are not exactly nine to five.
segments.zh: 正如你所知道的，丽贝卡，在新闻工作中的工作时间并不完全是九点到五点。

segments.en: You could be on call at any time but we do have to work very unsociable hours at times.
segments.zh: 你随时可能需要待命，而且有时得在深夜、周末等不便社交的时段工作。

segments.en: Well I'm used to that Mr Parsons.
segments.zh: 好吧，我已经习惯了帕森斯先生。

segments.en: So that's not really a shock for me.
segments.zh: 所以这对我来说并不是一个真正的震惊。

segments.en: Good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: As long as you understand that.
segments.zh: 只要你明白这一点。

segments.en: And when do you need to fill the vacancy Mr Parsons?
segments.zh: 帕森斯先生，您希望这个职位的人选什么时候到岗？

segments.en: Yesterday but no.
segments.zh: 最好昨天就到岗！不过，说正经的……

segments.en: We're hoping to start from the beginning of next month.
segments.zh: 我们希望从下个月初开始。

segments.en: That sounds ideal.
segments.zh: 听起来很理想。

segments.en: Alright we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So it's obviously a very difficult job and she asked some very key questions.
segments.zh: 所以这显然是一项非常困难的工作，她问了一些非常关键的问题。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at a couple of the words and phrases used there on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不看看语言要点中使用的几个单词和短语。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first word that we have here for Language Takeaway is workforce.
segments.zh: 我们在这里为语言要点提供的第一个词是劳动力。

segments.en: That's right a workforce.
segments.zh: 没错，就是劳动力。

segments.en: The company's workforce.
segments.zh: 公司的劳动力。

segments.en: And that basically means all the employees that we have working for us.
segments.zh: 这基本上是指所有为我们工作的员工。

segments.en: That might not be in one office.
segments.zh: 那可能不在一个办公室。

segments.en: Many companies have two, three, even a hundred offices.
segments.zh: 许多公司有两个、三个甚至一百个办公室。

segments.en: So the workforce means all the people who work for the company combined.
segments.zh: 因此，劳动力意味着为公司工作的所有人加起来。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a workforce.
segments.zh: 所以是劳动力。

segments.en: And well she asked about the workforce and well it's obviously a pretty big company.
segments.zh: 好吧，她问到了劳动力，这显然是一家相当大的公司。

segments.en: 150 employees.
segments.zh: 150 名员工。

segments.en: But he also mentioned that the news desk staff in Hong Kong comprises around 80 people or 80 staff.
segments.zh: 但他也提到，香港的新闻台工作人员约有 80 人或 80 名工作人员。

segments.en: So this verb to comprise or in this case it comprises means to make up or to account for.
segments.zh: 所以这个动词 to comprise，在这里是 it comprises，意思是 make up 或 account for，也就是“构成、占”。

segments.en: It's a very nice word to say it accounts for, it makes up, it's the total.
segments.zh: 用它来表达 account for、make up 很好，就是“总计”的意思。

segments.en: It's the total right.
segments.zh: 这是完全正确的。

segments.en: So in this case the news desk staff has 80 people.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，新闻台工作人员有 80 人。

segments.en: That's a very easy way to say it.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常简单的表达方式。

segments.en: But we could say it comprises 80 people.
segments.zh: 但我们可以说它包括 80 人。

segments.en: It sounds a bit better.
segments.zh: 听起来好一点。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So now obviously she's going to be a reporter or a journalist and he said that she should be on call at any time.
segments.zh: 所以现在显然她将成为一名记者或新闻工作者，他说她应该随时待命。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: On call is a phrase that we often hear with jobs like journalism but also medicine.
segments.zh: on call 这个短语，我们常在新闻业、医疗等职业中听到。

segments.en: So doctors have to be on call very often.
segments.zh: 所以医生必须经常随叫随到。

segments.en: This means that you don't have to be in the office but you have to be available to come into the office.
segments.zh: 这意味着您不必在办公室，但您必须有空进入办公室。

segments.en: So when someone calls you and they say we have an emergency you have to be available.
segments.zh: 因此，当有人打电话给您并且他们说我们有紧急情况时，您必须有空。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And you see it in movies all the time.
segments.zh: 你总是在电影中看到它。

segments.en: You know doctors are on call and maybe they're already sleeping or maybe they're out I don't know playing soccer with their kids and they receive a phone call and they have to go to the hospital in that moment.
segments.zh: 你知道医生在待命，也许他们已经在睡觉，或者他们出去了，我不知道和他们的孩子一起踢足球，他们接到一个电话，他们必须在那一刻去医院。

segments.en: It's because they're on call.
segments.zh: 这是因为他们随叫随到。

segments.en: That's because they're on call.
segments.zh: 那是因为他们随叫随到。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And so obviously this is a very difficult thing for someone.
segments.zh: 显然，这对某人来说是一件非常困难的事情。

segments.en: And he explains that the work has very unsociable hours at times.
segments.zh: 他解释说，这份工作有时得在很不合社交的时段上班。

segments.en: Okay so you can say that the hours are unsociable.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说这些时段很不合社交。

segments.en: You can also say that a person is unsociable.
segments.zh: 你也可以说一个人是不善交际的。

segments.en: It basically means that it's not very convenient for being a social person or for going out with friends and having many events to go to or fun things to do in your personal life.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着成为一个社交的人或与朋友出去玩，在你的个人生活中有很多活动要做或有趣的事情不是很方便。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if a person is unsociable it means that maybe that person is not very outgoing or maybe is always angry or grumpy so that person doesn't get along well with others.
segments.zh: 因此，如果一个人不善于交际，这意味着可能那个人不是很外向，或者可能总是生气或脾气暴躁，因此那个人与他人相处得不好。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So in this case it doesn't mean that it's a grumpy job.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，这并不意味着它是一个脾气暴躁的工作。

segments.en: It just means that because she might have to work at night very often or on the weekends it's very hard to have a social life.
segments.zh: 这只是意味着因为她可能不得不经常在晚上或周末工作，所以很难过上社交生活。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay so obviously this job is very difficult but in the end she was really happy with it and she said that sounds ideal, her starting time.
segments.zh: 好吧，很明显这份工作非常困难，但最终她真的很满意，她说这听起来很理想，她的开始时间。

segments.en: So something is ideal if it's perfect or great or the top.
segments.zh: 因此，如果它是完美的、伟大的或顶部的，那么它就是理想的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Many people talk about the ideal job, right?
segments.zh: 很多人谈论理想的工作，对吧？

segments.en: The perfect job.
segments.zh: 完美的工作。

segments.en: So that's the job that you have in your mind when you think of what is the best.
segments.zh: 所以当你想到什么是最好的时，这就是你脑海中的工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe my ideal job is different from your ideal job.
segments.zh: 所以也许我的理想工作与你理想的工作不同。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you have ideal jobs or your ideal house or your dream house.
segments.zh: 所以你有理想的工作、你理想的房子或你梦想中的房子。

segments.en: Your ideal husband.
segments.zh: 你理想的丈夫。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So ideal, idealism.
segments.zh: 如此理想，理想主义。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不再听一次对话。

segments.en: Let's review what Rebecca and Mr. Parsons talked about and we'll be back in a little bit with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 让我们回顾一下 Rebecca 和 Parsons 先生谈到的内容，稍后我们会带着流利表达回来。

segments.en: Could you tell me a little about the organization?
segments.zh: 你能告诉我一些关于这个组织的信息吗？

segments.en: For example, how big is your office here?
segments.zh: 例如，您的办公室有多大？

segments.en: Well, in total we have around 150 employees based in Hong Kong with another 400 in our head office in Beijing.
segments.zh: 总的来说，我们有约 150 名员工常驻香港，另外 400 人在北京总部。

segments.en: The news desk staff in Hong Kong has around 80 staff.
segments.zh: 香港的新闻台工作人员约有80名员工。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: And how about the working hours?
segments.zh: 工作时间怎么样？

segments.en: Well, as you know Rebecca, in journalism work hours are not exactly 9 to 5.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你所知道的，丽贝卡，在新闻工作中的工作时间并不完全是 9 到 5。

segments.en: You could be on call at any time, but we do have to work very unsociable hours at times.
segments.zh: 你可能随时需要待命，但我们有时不得不在很不合社交的时段工作。

segments.en: Well, I'm used to that Mr. Parsons.
segments.zh: 好吧，我已经习惯了帕森斯先生。

segments.en: So that's not really a shock for me.
segments.zh: 所以这对我来说并不是一个真正的震惊。

segments.en: Good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: As long as you understand that.
segments.zh: 只要你明白这一点。

segments.en: And when do you need to fill the vacancy Mr. Parsons?
segments.zh: 帕森斯先生，你什么时候需要填补这个空缺？

segments.en: Yesterday, but no.
segments.zh: 最好昨天！不过，说正经的……

segments.en: We're hoping to start from the beginning of next month.
segments.zh: 我们希望从下个月初开始。

segments.en: That sounds ideal.
segments.zh: 听起来很理想。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now we have four phrases for you prepared on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 因此，现在我们为您准备了关于流利表达的四个短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: This first phrase is something that we say all the time in English, but I think a lot of learners make mistakes when they use it.
segments.zh: 第一个短语是我们一直用英语说的话，但我认为很多学习者在使用它时都会犯错误。

segments.en: The phrase is how about.
segments.zh: 这个短语就是 how about。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you see that Rebecca was listening to what Mr. Parsons said and she said, and how about the working hours?
segments.zh: 所以你看到丽贝卡在听帕森斯先生的话，她说，工作时间怎么样？

segments.en: So this is a way to say, and what are the working hours?
segments.zh: 所以这是一种说法，工作时间是什么？

segments.en: But basically it's a way to continue the conversation.
segments.zh: 但基本上这是一种继续对话的方式。

segments.en: You can say this in many different ways, but it basically means, and what about?
segments.zh: 你可以用许多不同的方式说这个，但它基本上意味着，那又如何呢？

segments.en: Or, please tell me about.
segments.zh: 或者，请告诉我。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Now remember that many English learners mistake the phrase how about as if they were saying, how are you?
segments.zh: 记住，很多英语学习者会误把 how about 当成好像在说 how are you？

segments.en: Or how is it?
segments.zh: 或者怎么样？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: You have to be following someone else in the conversation.
segments.zh: 你必须在谈话中跟随别人。

segments.en: So for example, I could say, you know what?
segments.zh: 例如，我可以说，你知道吗？

segments.en: I'm going to have a hamburger with bacon.
segments.zh: 我要吃培根的汉堡包。

segments.en: How about you Marco?
segments.zh: 马可呢？

segments.en: What are you going to eat?
segments.zh: 你要吃什么？

segments.en: How about you buy me a cheeseburger?
segments.zh: 你给我买一个芝士汉堡怎么样？

segments.en: Okay, so this is basically a way of saying, okay, well maybe I'll have a cheeseburger or what are you going to have?
segments.zh: 好吧，这基本上是一种说法，好吧，也许我会吃芝士汉堡，或者你要吃什么？

segments.en: So now it's important to say, don't ever make this question.
segments.zh: 所以现在重要的是要说，永远不要提出这个问题。

segments.en: Don't ever ask, how about your weekend?
segments.zh: 永远不要问，你的周末怎么样？

segments.en: No, no, no, no, no.
segments.zh: 不，不，不，不，不。

segments.en: How was your weekend?
segments.zh: 你的周末过得怎么样？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: My weekend was great.
segments.zh: 我的周末很棒。

segments.en: How about yours?
segments.zh: 你的呢？

segments.en: How about yours?
segments.zh: 你的呢？

segments.en: That's continuing the conversation saying, mine was good.
segments.zh: 这继续说，我的很好。

segments.en: How was yours?
segments.zh: 你的怎么样？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what did he say?
segments.zh: 那么他说了什么？

segments.en: He said that when they were talking about the work hours, he said that the work hours are not exactly nine to five.
segments.zh: 他说，当他们谈论工作时间时，他说工作时间并不完全是九点到五点。

segments.en: Okay, so this is a kind of a set phrase we use often in English because a lot of people traditionally have worked from 9am to 5pm.
segments.zh: 好的，所以这是我们在英语中经常使用的一种固定短语，因为很多人传统上都从上午 9 点到下午 5 点工作。

segments.en: They have a break at lunch, then they go home.
segments.zh: 他们午餐休息，然后回家。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is a kind of measure for, this is a way to describe traditional working hours or traditional jobs.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种衡量标准，这是一种描述传统工作时间或传统工作的方式。

segments.en: So you can say, yeah, I have a really nice nine to five job.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，是的，我有一份非常好的朝九晚五的工作。

segments.en: You could say, I really don't want to work a nine to five job.
segments.zh: 你可以说，我真的不想从事朝九晚五的工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you don't want a traditional job where you're working from nine to five.
segments.zh: 所以你不想要一份朝九晚五的传统工作。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Most people I think work a little bit longer than that, but this is just a way of saying a traditional job.
segments.zh: 我认为大多数人的工作时间比这要长一点，但这只是说传统工作的一种方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Nine to five job.
segments.zh: 朝九晚五的工作。

segments.en: Now, why don't we move on to Rebecca saying that she is used to working long hours or being on call.
segments.zh: 现在，我们为什么不转向丽贝卡说她习惯长时间工作或待命。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this construction, to be used to, I'm used to doing this, is a way to say that I already do this.
segments.zh: 所以这个结构，习惯于，我习惯了这样做，是一种说我已经这样做的方式。

segments.en: This is my experience or I have the habit of working unusual hours.
segments.zh: 这是我的经验，或者我有工作不寻常的时间的习惯。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe for example, you live in a very noisy area in your neighborhood and somebody comes and visits you and they can't sleep because it's so noisy.
segments.zh: 例如，也许你住在附近一个非常嘈杂的地方，有人来拜访你，他们睡不着，因为它太吵了。

segments.en: You are used to it.
segments.zh: 你已经习惯了。

segments.en: Oh, you say, Oh, I don't mind.
segments.zh: 哦，你说，哦，我不介意。

segments.en: I'm used to the noise.
segments.zh: 我习惯了噪音。

segments.en: But your friend who's visiting is not used to it.
segments.zh: 但是你来访的朋友不习惯。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: They don't have this noise at home.
segments.zh: 他们家里没有这种噪音。

segments.en: So that's what happens and it can't sleep.
segments.zh: 所以这就是发生的事情，它无法入睡。

segments.en: So when you are used to something, you have the habit or you're accustomed to it.
segments.zh: 所以当你习惯了某事时，你有习惯，或者你已经习惯了它。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And what about our last phrase?
segments.zh: 最后一个短语是什么呢？

segments.en: Our last phrase comes at the end and Rebecca is talking about the start date for this job.
segments.zh: 我们的最后一句话出现在结尾，丽贝卡正在谈论这项工作的开始日期。

segments.en: She wants to know, when do you need to fill the vacancy?
segments.zh: 她想知道，你什么时候需要填补空缺？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: To fill the vacancy.
segments.zh: 填补空缺。

segments.en: Now, we have this word vacancy and that means that it's available, right?
segments.zh: 现在，我们有这个词空缺，这意味着它是可用的，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So vacancy is an available thing.
segments.zh: 所以空缺是一个可用的东西。

segments.en: It could be a vacant place.
segments.zh: 这可能是一个空置的地方。

segments.en: Like an apartment?
segments.zh: 像公寓一样？

segments.en: Like an apartment.
segments.zh: 像公寓一样。

segments.en: In this case, a vacancy in a company.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，公司有空缺。

segments.en: That means a job that is available.
segments.zh: 这意味着可用的工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So she is asking when she can fill the vacancy.
segments.zh: 所以她在问什么时候可以填补空缺。

segments.en: So we use the verb fill, to fill a vacancy.
segments.zh: 所以我们用动词填充来填补空缺。

segments.en: And this sounds a lot better than saying, Hey, when do I start working here?
segments.zh: 这听起来比说，嘿，我什么时候开始在这里工作要好得多？

segments.en: This is a polite way to say, when is the job going to begin?
segments.zh: 这是一种礼貌的方式，说工作什么时候开始？

segments.en: When do you need to fill the vacancy by?
segments.zh: 什么时候需要填补空缺？

segments.en: I guess another way of saying it would be, when is the starting date?
segments.zh: 我想另一种说法是，开始日期是什么时候？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: So as we say, also fill the vacancy is a very good option.
segments.zh: 所以正如我们所说，填补空缺也是一个非常好的选择。

segments.en: But don't say, when do I start working?
segments.zh: 但不要说，我什么时候开始工作？

segments.en: Or when do we start?
segments.zh: 或者我们什么时候开始？

segments.en: Yeah, no, we can talk about that in a minute.
segments.zh: 对，不，我们待会儿再聊这个。

segments.en: Let's listen first to our dialogue one more time.
segments.zh: 让我们先再听一次我们的对话。

segments.en: We'll be back shortly.
segments.zh: 我们很快就会回来。

segments.en: Could you tell me a little about the organization?
segments.zh: 你能告诉我一些关于这个组织的信息吗？

segments.en: For example, how big is your office here?
segments.zh: 例如，您的办公室有多大？

segments.en: Well, in total we have around 150 employees based in Hong Kong, with another 400 in our head office in Beijing.
segments.zh: 总的来说，我们有约 150 名员工常驻香港，另外 400 人在北京总部。

segments.en: The news desk staff in Hong Kong has around 80 staff.
segments.zh: 香港的新闻台工作人员约有80名员工。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: And how about the working hours?
segments.zh: 工作时间怎么样？

segments.en: Well, as you know, Rebecca, in journalism, work hours are not exactly nine to five.
segments.zh: 好吧，如你所知，丽贝卡，在新闻业，工作时间并不完全是九点到五点。

segments.en: You could be on call at any time.
segments.zh: 您可以随时随叫随到。

segments.en: But we do have to work very unsociable hours at times.
segments.zh: 但我们有时不得不在很不合社交的时段工作。

segments.en: Well, I'm used to that, Mr. Parsons.
segments.zh: 好吧，我已经习惯了，帕森斯先生。

segments.en: So that's not really a shock for me.
segments.zh: 所以这对我来说并不是一个真正的震惊。

segments.en: Good, as long as you understand that.
segments.zh: 很好，只要你明白这一点。

segments.en: And when do you need to fill the vacancy, Mr. Parsons?
segments.zh: 帕森斯先生，你什么时候需要填补空缺？

segments.en: Yesterday, but no, we are hoping to start from the beginning of next month.
segments.zh: 昨天，但不，我们希望从下个月初开始。

segments.en: That sounds ideal.
segments.zh: 听起来很理想。

segments.en: So talking about working hours, being on call or unsociable working hours, have you ever had a job where you've had to work maybe through the night?
segments.zh: 所以说到工作时间、随叫随到或不合时宜的工作时间，你有没有一份工作，你可能整晚都必须工作？

segments.en: Yes, I used to work in a movie theater when I was in college.
segments.zh: 是的，我上大学的时候曾经在电影院工作。

segments.en: I had a day job too, so it was kind of a mess.
segments.zh: 我也有一份日常工作，所以有点乱。

segments.en: I was very unsociable.
segments.zh: 我非常不善于交际。

segments.en: But I worked at a movie theater and I would start working at 6 p.m. or 5 p.m. and I would work until 2 or 3 a.m.
segments.zh: 但我在一家电影院工作，从下午 5 点或 6 点开始上班，一直工作到凌晨 2 点或 3 点。

segments.en: And so it was always busiest on Friday and Saturday.
segments.zh: 所以周五和周六总是最忙碌的。

segments.en: And so I could never go out with my friends.
segments.zh: 所以我永远不能和我的朋友出去。

segments.en: So while everyone was partying, you were at the movie theater.
segments.zh: 所以当每个人都在聚会时，你在电影院。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Or they would come to the movies and I would sneak in and bring them popcorn.
segments.zh: 或者他们来看电影，我会溜进去给他们送爆米花。

segments.en: So these unusual working hours, it's very interesting because usually, although it is a little bit more of a sacrifice, they usually pay a little bit better, right?
segments.zh: 所以这些不寻常的工作时间很有趣，因为通常虽然这多少算是一种牺牲，但薪水往往也会好一点，对吧？

segments.en: They do and there are some advantages.
segments.zh: 确实如此，而且还有一些好处。

segments.en: It means that you get to sleep in really late.
segments.zh: 这意味着你可以睡到很晚才起床。

segments.en: You don't have to wake up early.
segments.zh: 你不必早起。

segments.en: And you have the day off, like the entire day to do something.
segments.zh: 你休息一天，就像一整天做某事。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: What about you?
segments.zh: 你呢？

segments.en: Have you ever worked unusual hours?
segments.zh: 你有没有工作过不寻常的时间？

segments.en: Yes, yes.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: I used to work for a newspaper and obviously people like their newspaper in the mornings.
segments.zh: 我以前为一家报社工作，显然人们喜欢早上读报纸。

segments.en: So bright and early.
segments.zh: 所以就是一大清早。

segments.en: Bright and early.
segments.zh: 一大清早。

segments.en: We're talking about 6 a.m.
segments.zh: 我们说的是早上 6 点。

segments.en: So obviously, we would deliver the newspapers around 1 a.m., 2 a.m.
segments.zh: 很明显，我们会在凌晨 1 点、凌晨 2 点左右送报。

segments.en: From 1 a.m. to about 6 a.m.
segments.zh: 从凌晨1点到早上6点左右。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: So yeah, pretty unusual and very difficult because, for example, some people, for them, it's great to see the sunrise.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，非常不寻常且非常困难，因为例如，有些人，对于他们来说，很高兴看到日出。

segments.en: I've seen so many sunrises and it's not really romantic for me anymore.
segments.zh: 我看过这么多日出，对我来说不再浪漫了。

segments.en: We would call you a night owl.
segments.zh: 我们会称你为夜猫子。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Someone who's more awake at night.
segments.zh: 晚上更清醒的人。

segments.en: That's right and I still am.
segments.zh: 没错，我仍然是。

segments.en: So we're really interested to know maybe if you had any unusual working hours.
segments.zh: 所以我们真的很想知道你是否有任何不寻常的工作时间。

segments.en: Or do you work a 9 to 5?
segments.zh: 还是你在朝九晚五工作？

segments.en: Yeah, do you have a 9 to 5 job?
segments.zh: 是的，你有朝九晚五的工作吗？

segments.en: So come to our website EnglishPod.com, let us know and we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 所以来我们的网站 EnglishPod.com，告诉我们，我们会在那儿等着大家。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。
